1.w: Better is a dry crust of bread where there is quietness than a house full of feasting with strife.

2.w: A servant who acts wisely will rule over an heir who behaves shamefully and will share the inheritance along with the relatives.

3.w: The crucible is for refining silver and the furnace is for gold; likewise the Lord tests hearts.

4.w: One who acts wickedly pays attention to evil counsel; a liar listens to a malicious tongue.

5.w: The one who mocks the poor has insulted his Creator; whoever rejoices over disaster will not go unpunished.

6.w: Grandchildren are like a crown to the elderly, and the glory of children is their parents.

7.w: Excessive speech is not becoming for a fool; how much less are lies for a ruler!

8.w: A bribe works like a charm for the one who offers it; in whatever he does he succeeds.

9.w: The one who forgives an offense seeks love, but whoever repeats a matter separates close friends.

10.w: A rebuke makes a greater impression on a discerning person than a hundred blows on a fool.

11.w: An evil person seeks only rebellion, and so a cruel messenger will be sent against him.

12.w: It is better for a person to meet a mother bear being robbed of her cubs than to encounter a fool in his folly.

13.w: As for the one who repays evil for good, evil will not leave his house.

14.w: Starting a quarrel is like letting out water; abandon strife before it breaks out!

15.w: The one who acquits the guilty and the one who condemns the innocent — both of them are an abomination to the Lord.

16.w: What’s the point of a fool having money in hand to buy wisdom when his head is empty?

17.w: A friend loves at all times, and a relative is born to help in adversity.

18.w: The one who lacks sense strikes hands in pledge and puts up financial security for his neighbor.

19.w: The one who loves a quarrel loves transgression; whoever builds his gate high seeks destruction.

20.w: The one who has a perverse heart does not find good, and the one who is deceitful in speech falls into trouble.

21.w: Whoever brings a fool into the world does so to his grief, and the father of a fool has no joy.

22.w: A cheerful heart brings good healing, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.

23.w: A wicked person receives a bribe secretly to pervert the ways of justice.

24.w: Wisdom is directly in front of the discerning person, but the eyes of a fool run to the ends of the earth.

25.w: A foolish child is a grief to his father and bitterness to the mother who bore him.

26.w: It is terrible to punish a righteous person, and to flog honorable men is wrong.

27.w: The truly wise person restrains his words, and the one who stays calm is discerning.

28.w: Even a fool who remains silent is considered wise, and the one who holds his tongue is deemed discerning.
